input.command: python3 -c 'import pathlib, duckdb, matplotlib.pyplot as plt; p="data/crashes.parquet"; q="select year(crash_date) as year, sum(coalesce(number_of_motorist_killed,0)) as motorist_fatalities from read_parquet(?) where year(crash_date) between 2013 and 2025 group by 1 order by 1"; df=duckdb.connect().execute(q,[p]).df(); out=pathlib.Path("out"); out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); df.to_csv(out/"values.csv",index=False); fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(10,5.6)); ax.plot(df["year"],df["motorist_fatalities"],color="#2166ac",marker="o",linewidth=2.4,markersize=6); ax.set_title("Annual motorist fatalities in NYC crashes (2013–2025)",fontsize=15,weight="bold",pad=15); ax.set_ylabel("Motorists killed (count)"); ax.set_xlabel("Crash year"); ax.set_xticks(df["year"]); ax.tick_params(axis="x",rotation=35); ax.grid(axis="y",alpha=.25); ax.spines[["top","right"]].set_visible(False); ax.annotate("110",(2013,110),xytext=(0,9),textcoords="offset points",ha="center",fontsize=9); ax.annotate("81",(2025,81),xytext=(0,9),textcoords="offset points",ha="center",fontsize=9); fig.text(.5,.015,"Crash counts show fatalities, not risk per mile; vehicle-miles traveled are not in this dataset.",ha="center",fontsize=9,color="#444444"); fig.tight_layout(rect=(0,.05,1,1)); fig.savefig(out/"initial.png",dpi=180,bbox_inches="tight"); print(df.to_string(index=False)); print("Saved out/initial.png and out/values.csv")'

part.text:
Chart saved to `./out/initial.png`; plotted data saved to `./out/values.csv`.

ANSWER: The data can’t tell us whether the risk per mile declined because it has no miles-driven measure. Annual motorist fatalities fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (about 26%), but they fluctuated substantially in between.
